title: Panorama stitching and multi-zone post-processing for landscape scenes (Expedition 2-13)

date.basis: Embedded creation time suggests approximate export date; transcript indicates a single-session workflow around panorama creation and heavy post-processing.

summary: The video documents a landscape photography workflow focused on building a wide panorama from multiple frames, managing dynamic range, and sculpting light and texture through layered, zone-based editing. A presenter compares composition options, explains panorama capture and stitching concepts, then demonstrates sky replacement via clone stamping, selective dehazing, and targeted brightness/contrast adjustments to separate and refine foreground, midground, and background. The session covers non-destructive versioning, creative sky augmentation (a “cheating” sky extension), RAW workflow considerations, and final color grading before export, with practical tips for edge quality, print readiness, and workflow efficiency.
topics: Panorama stitching workflow (capture, merge, export as TIFF)
Panoramic distortion vs rectilinear distortion; wide-field planning
Leading lines and convergence for composition in landscape
Sky replacement and sky cloning with hard-edge brush and clone stamp
Edge refinement, masking, and feathered fades to avoid artifacts
Dehaze, warmth, and color grading across image zones
Layer separation and light bleed to simulate sunrise reflections
Non-destructive editing and versioning (saving multiple states)
Creative sky extension (sky size manipulation and beam enhancement)
RAW workflow considerations and file compatibility (CR3)
Final polish: texture/clarity, selective color, export considerations

sections.title: Initial composition evaluation and leading-light strategy
sections.description: The presenter compares frame options to steer the viewer toward the light, notes how light placement and converging leading lines affect composition, and discusses initial framing decisions.

sections.title: Panorama plan and data handling
sections.description: Cueing the workflow for panorama work, including locating the panoramic sequence on storage and considering how multiple frames will be stitched.

sections.title: Wide-field capture concepts and exposure planning
sections.description: Discusses using a panorama feature to create a wide-angle look, the typical shot count for a broad field of view, and the implications for distortion and later rectilinear correction.

sections.title: Export steps and initial view preparation
sections.description: Describes exporting the panorama as a TIFF and saving it to the desktop to avoid card-based processing delays, followed by initial viewing and cropping considerations.

sections.title: Sky enhancement: cloning sky for focal emphasis
sections.description: Demonstrates cloning sky into the scene to reinforce the horizon and sky treatment, with careful edge work and gradual fades to maintain realism.

sections.title: Light bleed, dehaze, and edge refinement for sunrise effect
sections.description: Explains leveraging dehaze and controlled light bleed to simulate sunrise illumination on mountains, while refining edges to ensure print-quality boundaries.

sections.title: Zone-based processing and preliminary separation
sections.description: Introduces dividing the image into zones and using targeted adjustments (textures, whites, curves, color grading) to separate and manage different parts of the scene.

sections.title: Per-zone processing routine and integration
sections.description: Details a workflow for processing each zone individually and then recombining, with emphasis on preserving sky contrast while enriching foreground texture and color harmony.

sections.title: Versioning and remixing workflow
sections.description: Shows how to preserve multiple editing states to compare variations and blend ideas from different versions for the final result.

sections.title: Creative sky-augmentation and practical constraints
sections.description: Demonstrates a ‘cheating’ technique to enlarge sky beams by increasing sky size and selectively transferring beams, while acknowledging the need to later merge with additional panoramas and preserve consistent seams.

sections.title: RAW compatibility, final color grading, and export options
concepts: final color grading (shadows, blacks, whites, balance)
sections.description: Addresses RAW file compatibility concerns, demonstrates finishing color grading and selective color tuning, and discusses export paths and post-processing tools, ending with notes about ongoing computer-related workflow issues.

featured_techniques.technique: Sky replacement using clone stamp and hard-edge brush
Layer-based zone separation and light bleed
Dehaze and color grading for multi-zone editing
Creative sky extension (beams) via sky enlargement
Final polish: texture/clarity and selective color in midtone regions
